newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schmalbach-Lubeca buys Johnson's PET unit.
newsitem.headline: Schmalbach-Lubeca buys Johnson's PET unit.

text.p: German packaging producer Schmalbach-Lubeca AG, a unit of utility giant Viag AG said on Monday it would take over U.S. group Johnson Controls Inc's PET unit at the start of 1997 for about one billion marks ($645.6 million).
The one billion mark figure named in media reports "is not completely wrong", said Schmalbach finance director Jan Maarten Henderson, but declined to be more specific.
Schmalbach plans no capital increase to finance the purchase of the U.S. plastics maker.

The formation of a joint venture between Schmalbach's metal packaging division with Pechiney and Doughty Hanson will finance part of the PET purchase, and the rest will come from bank loans, Henderson said.
The metal packaging unit had 1995 sales of 1.1 billion marks. It will be 100 percent integrated in the joint venture, in which Schmalbach will hold a 20 percent stake.
In a mandatory statement, Schmalbach Lubeca said the PET unit had sales of 1.2 billion marks in 1996 and around 2,300 staff.
Terms were not disclosed. Schmalbach Lubeca said final contract details and cartel office approval were still outstanding.
The acquisition would advance its aim to become a leading producer of PET applications, the German firm said, adding that it expected its sales in this area to reach around 1.9 billion marks in 1997.

Schmalbach sees its own sales flat this year at about four billion marks, compared with 4.124 billion last year, chairman Hanno Fiedler said. The company recently forecast its 1996 profit at 50 million marks.
This should form the basis for a return to a dividend payout at the 1994 level of five marks a share.
